title: MCP server | WP Waterfall Docs
snippet:
The WP Waterfall MCP server at https://mcp.wpwaterfall.com lets Claude, Claude Code, Cursor, ChatGPT, or another AI assistant look at your sites and change them, always as you and never with more access than you have.
The WP Waterfall MCP server lets an AI assistant look at your WP Waterfall sites and change them. It speaks the Model Context Protocol to the assistant and the public WP Waterfall API to WP Waterfall, holds no data of its own, and acts as the person who approved it, so it can never do more than you can.
## What is the server address?
```
https://mcp.wpwaterfall.com
```
Add it as a remote server (Streamable HTTP) with OAuth sign-in. You need no API key and nothing to install. The **Connections** tab of **Integrations** shows the address with a copy button while no app is connected.
## How do I connect an assistant?
| Client | What to do |
|---|---|
| Claude (web, desktop, and mobile) | Open **Settings**, then **Connectors**, then **Add custom connector**. Name it WP Waterfall and paste the address. Steps: [Claude Desktop](https://docs.wpwaterfall.com/mcp/claude-desktop). |
| Claude Code | Run `claude mcp add --transport http wpwaterfall https://mcp.wpwaterfall.com`, then run `/mcp` and choose **Authenticate** for wpwaterfall. Steps: [Claude Code](https://docs.wpwaterfall.com/mcp/claude-code). |
| Cursor | Add `{"mcpServers": {"wpwaterfall": {"url": "https://mcp.wpwaterfall.com"}}}` to `~/.cursor/mcp.json`, then choose **Connect** next to wpwaterfall. Steps: [Cursor](https://docs.wpwaterfall.com/mcp/cursor). |
| ChatGPT | Turn on developer mode in **Settings**, then **Connectors**, then **Advanced**. Create a connector, paste the address, and choose OAuth for sign in. Which plans offer this depends on OpenAI. |
| Any other client | Choose a remote server (Streamable HTTP) with OAuth sign in and paste the address. |
## What does approving do?
The assistant opens a WP Waterfall sign-in page. You sign in, pick the company, and choose **Approve** or **Deny** on one screen, with an **Access** choice of **Full access** (the default) or **Read only**. A read only connection can look at your sites, logs, and settings but cannot change anything: WP Waterfall refuses every tool that changes things, whatever the assistant asks. Full access is everything your role allows, and never more. Staff tools are never available this way. Integrations appears once your company has a plan. title: AI assistant setup | Made with Supernova
snippet:
Waterfall UI ships with [Model Context Protocol (MCP)](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/) server support so AI coding assistants (Claude Code, Cursor, Windsurf, etc.) can read design tokens, component props, and design files directly.
Connect to dv01 WDS’s MCP server
Install this context in your AI tool to get accurate data and knowledge about the entire waterfall design system.
In your AI tool of choice, add the following URL as a custom MCP connector:
```none
https://mcp.supernova.io/mcp/c/113356-dv01-wds
```
Connect to dv01 Writing’s MCP server
Install this context in your AI tool to get accurate data and knowledge about writing content for dv01 apps.
In your AI tool of choice, add the following URL as a custom MCP connector:
```none
https://mcp.supernova.io/mcp/c/304327-dv01-writing
```
## Quick setup
Add a .mcp.json file to the root of your project:
```json
{
"mcpServers": {
"waterfall-storybook": {
"type": "http",
"url": "https://waterfall-components.dv01.co/mcp"
},
"waterfall-supernova": {
"type": "http",
"url": "https://mcp.supernova.io/mcp/c/113356-dv01-wds"
},
"writing-content-supernova": {
"type": "http",
"url": "https://mcp.supernova.io/mcp/c/304327-writing"
},
"figma": {
"type": "http",
"url": "https://mcp.figma.com/mcp"
}
}
}
```
Restart your AI assistant. It will now have live access to Waterfall UI component docs, design system guidelines, writing guidelines, and Figma designs.
## Available MCP servers
| Server | URL | Use it for |
|---|---|---|
| **Storybook (hosted)** | https://waterfall-components.dv01.co/mcp | Component props, stories, and usage examples. Always available — no local setup. |
| **Storybook (local)** | http://localhost:6006/mcp | Same as above, but from your dev server. Use when contributing to Waterfall UI. Requires bun run storybook. |
| **Supernova WDS** | https://mcp.supernova.io/mcp/c/113356-dv01-wds | Design system documentation — tokens, components, patterns, accessibility. |
| **Supernova Writing** | https://mcp.supernova.io/mcp/c/304327-writing | Writing guidelines for dv01 apps — voice and tone, capitalization, punctuation, grammar. |
| **Figma** | https://mcp.figma.com/mcp | Read Figma files for design-to-code workflows. Requires Figma account access. |

title: @waterfallbridge/mcp
GitHub - databar-ai/databar-mcp-server: MCP server for Databar.ai — enables AI assistants to run data enrichments, manage tables, and more
snippet:
# Databar MCP Server
A [Model Context Protocol](https://modelcontextprotocol.io) (MCP) server that enables AI assistants like Claude to interact with [Databar.ai](https://databar.ai)'s data enrichment API. Discover, configure, and run data enrichments across hundreds of data providers using natural language.
## Features
- **Smart Enrichment Discovery** — Search and filter enrichments by keyword or category
- **Natural Language Interface** — Ask "get David's LinkedIn profile" and the right enrichment runs automatically
- **Bulk Operations** — Enrich many records in a single call with bulk enrichment and bulk waterfall support
- **Table Management** — Create tables, manage columns, insert/update/upsert rows
- **Waterfall Support** — Try multiple data providers sequentially until one succeeds
- **Async Handling** — Automatic polling for results with no manual intervention
- **Intelligent Caching** — 24-hour result cache reduces API calls and costs
- **Error Handling** — Retries with exponential backoff and clear error messages

```
git clone https://github.com/databar-ai/databar-mcp-server.git
cd databar-mcp-server
npm install
npm run build
```
### Configure Claude Desktop
Edit your Claude Desktop config file:
- **macOS**: `~/Library/Application Support/Claude/claude_desktop_config.json`
- **Windows**: `%APPDATA%\Claude\claude_desktop_config.json`
```
{
"mcpServers": {
"databar": {
"command": "node",
"args": ["/absolute/path/to/databar-mcp-server/dist/index.js"],
"env": {
"DATABAR_API_KEY": "your-api-key-here"
}
}
}
}
```

### Find an email using waterfall
> *"Find the email for John Smith at Google"*
Runs a waterfall that tries multiple providers until one returns a result.

## How It Works
### Async Task Handling
1. Server sends a run request to the Databar API
2. API returns a `task_id`
3. Server automatically polls `/v1/tasks/{task_id}` every 2 seconds
4. When status is `completed`, results are returned
5. If data has expired (1-hour retention), `gone` status is handled gracefully
### Caching
- Results are cached for 24 hours by default
- Cache key: enrichment ID + serialized params
- Cached results don't consume credits
- Use `skip_cache: true` to force fresh data
### Smart Categorization
Enrichments are automatically categorized (People, Company, Email, Phone, Social, Financial, Verification) to help the AI assistant pick the right tool.

title: Releases · modelcontextprotocol/servers
snippet:
## Security fixes
v2.5.0 fixes eight vulnerabilities in three servers. Upgrade `mcp-server-git` to 2026.11.18,
`@modelcontextprotocol/server-filesystem` to 2.4.0 and `@modelcontextprotocol/server-everything` to 2.3.1.
| Package | Affected | Fixed in |
|---|---|---|
| `mcp-server-git` | through 2026.11.11 | 2026.11.18 |
| `@modelcontextprotocol/server-filesystem` | all versions before 2.4.0, and date versions 2025.1.14 through 2026.8.31 | 2.4.0 |
| `@modelcontextprotocol/server-everything` | through 2.3.0 | 2.3.1 |

**How these servers stand**
- **The TypeScript servers rely on the Node.js runtime for certificate checks.** They ship no CA certificates of their own. Only `server-everything` makes outbound HTTPS requests (`gzip-file-as-resource`), and the Node.js it runs on verifies them. `server-filesystem`, `server-memory` and `server-sequential-thinking` make no network connections.
- **`mcp-server-fetch` verifies HTTPS against the `certifi` bundle**, through `httpx`. Installing from PyPI (`uvx mcp-server-fetch`, `pip install mcp-server-fetch`) resolves the current `certifi`, 2026.10.23 or later. The repository's `fetch` Dockerfile installs from its lockfile, which this release moves to `certifi` 2026.10.23 ([#5341](https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/servers/pull/5341)).
- **`mcp-server-git` and `mcp-server-time` make no network connections.**

## Python servers: changes for clients
`mcp-server-fetch`, `mcp-server-git` and `mcp-server-time` have no CHANGELOG, so here is what changes for a client in `2026.10.19`. They are now built on the MCP Python SDK's high-level `MCPServer` ([#5175](https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/servers/pull/5175)).
- **Unknown tool:** a JSON-RPC `-32602` error (`Unknown tool: <name>`) in both protocol eras, as the spec requires. It used to be an `isError` result.
- **Tool errors** read `Error executing tool <name>: <message>`. Argument-validation errors now use pydantic's wording. Both are still `isError` results.
- **Capabilities:** each server now advertises `prompts` and `resources` capabilities (with `listChanged: false`). fetch's `fetch` prompt is the only entry in those lists.
- **time:** `get_current_time` and `convert_time` declare an `outputSchema` and return `structuredContent`. The text content is unchanged.
- **fetch:** a `prompts/get` result's `description` is now always the prompt's registered description.
- **Requires** `mcp>=2.3,<3`.

title: GitHub - modelcontextprotocol/servers: Model Context Protocol Reference Servers
snippet:
# Model Context Protocol servers
This repository is a collection of *reference implementations* for the [Model Context Protocol](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/) (MCP), as well as references to community-built servers and additional resources.
Important
If you are looking for a list of MCP servers, you can browse published servers on [the MCP Registry](https://registry.modelcontextprotocol.io/). The repository served by this README is dedicated to housing just the small number of reference servers maintained by the MCP steering group.
Warning
The servers in this repository are intended as **reference implementations** to demonstrate MCP features and SDK usage. They are meant to serve as educational examples for developers building their own MCP servers, not as production-ready solutions. Developers should evaluate their own security requirements and implement appropriate safeguards based on their specific threat model and use case.
The servers in this repository showcase the versatility and extensibility of MCP, demonstrating how it can be used to give Large Language Models (LLMs) secure, controlled access to tools and data sources. Typically, each MCP server is implemented with an MCP SDK:
- [C# MCP SDK](https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/csharp-sdk)
- [Go MCP SDK](https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/go-sdk)
- [Java MCP SDK](https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/java-sdk)
- [Kotlin MCP SDK](https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/kotlin-sdk)
- [PHP MCP SDK](https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/php-sdk)
- [Python MCP SDK](https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/python-sdk)
- [Ruby MCP SDK](https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/ruby-sdk)
- [Rust MCP SDK](https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/rust-sdk)
- [Swift MCP SDK](https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/swift-sdk)
- [TypeScript MCP SDK](https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/typescript-sdk)
## 🌟 Reference Servers
These servers aim to demonstrate MCP features and the official SDKs.
- **[Everything](/modelcontextprotocol/servers/blob/main/src/everything)** - Reference / test server with prompts, resources, and tools.
- **[Fetch](/modelcontextprotocol/servers/blob/main/src/fetch)** - Web content fetching and conversion for efficient LLM usage.
- **[Filesystem](/modelcontextprotocol/servers/blob/main/src/filesystem)** - Secure file operations with configurable access controls.
